title: Water Storage
description: Elevated water held behind the concrete dam stores gravitational potential energy ready for controlled release.
engineeringExplanation: Water at headwater elevation above tailrace elevation possesses static gravitational potential proportional to gross head. Energy capacity depends on both stored volume and vertical elevation difference.
physicalProcess: Hydrostatic equilibrium inside the basin; dam monolith transfers horizontal water pressure thrust into bedrock foundation.
lossMechanismSummary: Evaporation/seepage outside short-term model; spillway bypass wastes potential energy if reservoir floods.
narrationText: Energy starts with elevation. By impounding river flow behind the dam, the reservoir holds water tens of meters above the powerhouse—turning quiet water volume into stored gravitational potential.

title: Water Intake
description: Submerged intake bellmouth draws filtered water smoothly past the trash rack and open intake gate into the headrace.
engineeringExplanation: Water accelerates gently from near-zero reservoir velocity through the trash rack bar screen into the flared concrete bellmouth. Smooth curvature minimizes entrance separation eddies while submergence prevents air-core vortices.
physicalProcess: Pressure-driven acceleration across bar screen and streamlined bellmouth contraction into closed conduit flow.
lossMechanismSummary: Trash-rack bar drag and bellmouth entrance eddy loss (K_e * v^2 / 2g).
narrationText: Before entering the powerhouse tunnels, water passes through the trash rack to filter out logs and stones, then accelerates smoothly around a curved concrete bellmouth past the open emergency intake gate.

title: Water Conveyance
description: Pressurized water travels through the headrace and pressure tunnel past the surge tank, descending the steel penstock to the main inlet valve.
engineeringExplanation: Inside the closed conduit, gravitational elevation drops rapidly down the inclined steel penstock while internal hydrostatic pressure rises sharply. The surge tank buffers water-hammer transients while conduit friction creates permanent head loss yielding Net Head (H) at turbine inlet.
physicalProcess: Confined incompressible pipe flow converting elevation head into high static pressure head + controlled kinetic velocity head, minus Darcy-Weisbach friction loss.
lossMechanismSummary: Darcy-Weisbach pipe wall friction, tunnel bends, and valve entrance losses (Delta H_loss).
narrationText: Descending the steel penstock concentrates elevation drop into intense hydraulic pressure—delivering full hydraulic power right to the open main inlet valve while the surge tank stands guard against pressure shock.

title: Turbine Conversion
description: Pressurized swirling water enters the spiral casing, throttles through pivoting guide vanes, and transfers angular momentum and pressure across the Francis runner blades.
engineeringExplanation: The tapering spiral casing distributes water evenly 360 degrees. Stay vanes carry structural load while pivoting guide vanes regulate discharge Q and inject optimal swirl angle. Inside the submerged Francis runner, pressure drops and water turns radial-to-axial, generating shaft torque per Euler's equation.
physicalProcess: Reaction and impulse hydrodynamic momentum transfer from pressurized swirling fluid to rotating double-curved blades.
lossMechanismSummary: Guide-vane throttling, blade incidence shock at off-BEP, friction, labyrinth seal leakage, and exit swirl into draft tube.
narrationText: Inside the spiral casing, water wraps evenly around the turbine, passes through pivoting guide vanes that act as both throttle and steering nozzle, and pushes against the twisted Francis blades to generate immense rotational torque.

title: Mechanical Transmission
description: The forged steel main shaft carries rotational torque vertically upward from the submerged runner through hydrodynamic bearings to the generator rotor.
engineeringExplanation: Pure mechanical power transmission (P_m = T * omega) bridges the wet hydraulic pit below and the dry electrical generator floor above. Tilting-pad thrust and guide bearings support axial hydraulic thrust and rotating mass on pressurized oil films.
physicalProcess: Torsional shear and axial thrust transmission along a synchronized rotating steel shaft supported by oil-film bearings.
lossMechanismSummary: Hydrodynamic bearing oil-film shear friction and shaft gland seal friction (~0.2-0.5%).
narrationText: The vertical steel main shaft delivers millions of Newton-meters of torque straight upward from the submerged turbine pit to the generator hall—floating smoothly inside oil-film thrust and guide bearings.

title: Electrical Generation
description: Energized salient poles on the spinning rotor sweep magnetic flux across stationary copper stator windings, inducing three-phase alternating current.
engineeringExplanation: DC current from the excitation system energizes 24 field windings on the salient-pole rotor. Locked at synchronous speed (250 rpm at 50 Hz), rotating flux cuts three-phase stator armature coils per Faraday's Law, generating AC power while coolers reject thermal losses.
physicalProcess: Electromechanical energy conversion via rotating magnetic field induction across the radial air gap.
lossMechanismSummary: Stator & field I^2R copper heating, laminated silicon-steel core hysteresis/eddy losses, rotor windage, and bearing drag.
narrationText: Inside the generator barrel, DC-excited rotor poles spin past stationary copper stator coils at an exact synchronous speed set by grid frequency—converting shaft rotation into three-phase AC electricity while coolers carry away heat losses.

title: Voltage Transformation
description: Generated power flows through isolated-phase busbars and the generator circuit breaker into the step-up transformer, boosting voltage dramatically for long-distance transmission.
engineeringExplanation: Electricity leaves the stator at high current (~2,400 A at 11 kV class). Passing through the synchronizing circuit breaker and step-up transformer increases voltage by over 10x (e.g., 11 kV to 132 kV) while cutting current proportionally, slashing transmission line I^2R heat losses by over 100x.
physicalProcess: Three-phase bus conduction, breaker synchronization protection, and mutual magnetic flux voltage transformation.
lossMechanismSummary: Busbar resistance drop plus transformer core magnetization and winding copper loss (~0.3-0.8%).
narrationText: Power cannot travel miles efficiently at 11,000 volts—massive current would overheat the wires. The step-up transformer boosts voltage more than tenfold, shrinking line current and slashing transmission losses by over a hundred times.

title: Power Transmission
description: High-voltage AC flows through the switchyard protection bay onto overhead ACSR transmission lines feeding the interconnected electrical grid.
engineeringExplanation: The outdoor switchyard provides HV circuit breaking, lightning surge protection, and isolation before energizing overhead ACSR lines. Delivered power tracks consumer load demand up to unit generation capacity, locked strictly to grid frequency.
physicalProcess: High-voltage three-phase electromagnetic power propagation across overhead transmission lines into the interconnected grid sink.
lossMechanismSummary: Overhead ACSR conductor I^2R Joule heating and corona losses along transmission corridor.
narrationText: Through the switchyard's high-voltage breakers and surge arresters, synchronized electricity enters overhead transmission lines—delivering clean power to cities and factories locked strictly to the grid's 50 Hz rhythm.

title: Water Discharge
description: Having given up its pressure and kinetic energy inside the Francis turbine, decelerated water exits the submerged draft tube outlet into the tailrace and rejoins the downstream river.
engineeringExplanation: The expanding draft tube gently decelerates runner outflow, recovering residual kinetic head so water exits calmly through the submerged outlet into the tailrace. Crucially, zero water is consumed: mass conservation guarantees Q_downstream equals Q_intake.
physicalProcess: Subcritical diffuser pressure recovery followed by calm open-channel discharge returning to natural river hydraulics.
lossMechanismSummary: Residual exit kinetic energy (v_out^2 / 2g) dissipated cleanly downstream; zero water volume consumed.
narrationText: Electricity has reached the grid, yet not a single liter of water was destroyed. Gently slowed by the draft tube, the river exits calmly through the tailrace—its gravitational energy harvested, its volume returned intact.
